title: Two-Ball Crossover Series
description: Stationary two-ball work where both balls swap hands — side-by-side, front crossovers and between-the-legs — for advanced handlers.

content.objective: Exchange two balls between the hands in timing, building coordination and a confident weak hand.
content.setup: Each player has two balls and a personal space.
instructions: Pound both balls together at knee height for 10 dribbles.
Front crossover: cross both balls in front, one bouncing slightly before the other.
Lateral swap: each ball bounces in front of the opposite foot, passing each other.
Between-the-legs: one ball goes between the legs while the other crosses in front.
Finish with 15 seconds of alternating dribbles as fast as possible.
coachingPoints: Stagger the two balls so they never collide.
Keep both balls below the waist.
commonMistakes: Crossing both balls at the same moment so they collide.
Standing up to save a ball.
Dribbling one ball much higher than the other.
content.safety: Plenty of space between players; loose balls retrieved only between rounds.
progressions: Add a cone pickup during the alternating set.
regressions: One ball and one tennis ball.
Two balls without crossovers, just pounds and alternates.
successCriteria: Ten clean swaps in a row for each exercise.
content.gameApplication: Two-ball coordination makes single-ball changes of hand feel easy and automatic under pressure.
